title: Strategic Leadership Digest and Renewal Touchmap
content:
Purpose
This is a one-page executive digest + lightweight playbook for customer-facing quarterly recaps and renewal runway conversations. Designed for fast prep before an exec-level sync and a companion customer-facing email. Use as the source of truth for the next quarter of sponsored touchpoints and decisioning.

Audience
Primary: Customer Executive Sponsor, VP/Product/Platform leaders at the account, and internal CSM/Account owners.

TL;DR (one-sentence summary)
- Customer is healthy with steady usage (+12% q/q), three adoption wins this quarter, renewal on track but requires decision on committed seats by month X to secure discount.

Three-minute talking points (for exec sync)
1) Value recap (30s): Key outcomes delivered this quarter (time to value, cost per inference improvements, reliability wins).
2) Signals (60s): Top metrics that matter — latency SLO attainment, top-10 API call types, cost per 1k tokens compared to last quarter, active users hitting heavy workloads.
3) Risk & ask (45s): The one ask (renewal commitment or prioritization of private deployment POC) and mitigation steps if not approved.
4) Next steps (30s): Concrete next actions and decision owner.

Prepared slide/one-pager structure (use for internal prep or to convert to slide)
- Header: Customer, Exec Sponsor, Date, CSM
- Page body: 6 blocks (Health Snapshot, Wins this Quarter, Usage & Economics, Risk & Mitigation, Renewal Runway, Next 90d Plan)
- Footer: Link to repo/Confluence + contact info (CSM, Solutions Eng lead)

Health Snapshot (short bullets to read aloud)
- Usage: 1.2M tokens generated this quarter (+12% q/q)
- Reliability: 99.75% API Uptime, P95 latency 210ms
- Cost signal: Avg cost per 1k tokens $0.85 (down from $0.95 q/q)
- Quality: Failure rate on reranking endpoints <0.5%

Top 3 wins (customer-facing framing)
1) Reduced inference cost by targeted batching/quantization recommendations (client saw ~11% reduction in prod token cost).
2) Rolled out model pinning for compliance-sensitive pipeline with zero downtime during cutover.
3) Built a small evaluation harness for prompt regressions — blocked a quality regression in July.

Renewal runway (concise tracker to surface at exec sync)
- Renewal window: 60 days prior to contract end date (Contract end: 2026-06-30)
- Current commitment ask: Move from pay-as-you-go to a 12-month reserved capacity at 20% discount if committed by 2026-05-15
- Impact if deferred: Pricing will revert to list for next quarter; potential capacity prioritization limitations during peak windows

Quick renewal action checklist (owner + due date)
- CSM: Send commercial summary + commitment scenarios to legal/buyer (Due: 2026-04-05)
- Solutions Eng: Deliver capacity sizing slide and data center latency map (Due: 2026-04-12)
- Customer Exec: Confirm decision owner and procurement timeline (Due: 2026-04-19)

Risk matrix (for exec conversation)
- Low probability / High impact: Procurement delays -> contingency: short-term bridge pricing + prioritized support during procurement
- Medium probability / Medium impact: Spike in peak usage -> contingency: burst capacity addendum + temporary throttle policy

Next 90-day roadmap (customer-facing bullets)
- Month 1: Complete Dedicated sizing review + finalize reserved capacity proposal
- Month 2: Pilot private deployment networking prep (if requested) + runload test for sustained throughput targets
- Month 3: Launch auto-fallback routing for critical flows; setup SLA dashboard alerts for execs

Email templates (ready-to-send customer-facing quarterly recap)
Subject options (pick one):
- "Q2 Recap & Renewal Options — Redwood + <Customer>"
- "Quarterly outcomes and next steps (action requested)"

Email body (concise, exec-friendly):
Hi <FirstName>,

Quick recap of the last quarter and an ask to keep on your radar:

1) Top outcomes: Reduced token costs (~11%), improved P95 latency (210ms), and successful model pin for compliance.
2) Health snapshot: 99.75% uptime, usage +12% q/q, quality metrics stable.
3) Renewal ask: To secure pricing and dedicated capacity, we recommend moving to a 12-month reserved capacity by 2026-05-15. Attached are three commitment scenarios (no-cost, moderate, committed).

Proposed next step: 15-minute sync week of <date> to walk through scenarios and procurement timeline.

Thanks,
<CSM Name>

Note: attach the one-page digest (this doc converted to PDF) and a short commit-vs-no-commit pricing table.

Customer-facing summary: 30–60 second script for exec to forward internally
- "We reduced our inference unit cost ~11% while cutting P95 latency — Redwood proposes a reserved option to lock in these economics. Let's decide by mid-May to secure pricing and priority capacity."

Playbook: escalation and follow-up cadence (for internal use)
- Day 0 (after exec sync): Update Confluence renewal page, create procurement tracker ticket (JIRA-CS-XXXX).
- Day 5: Send pricing scenarios and one-pager; confirm decision owner.
- Week 3: If no firm reply, run risk playbook (schedule Solutions Eng deep-dive and prepare bridge pricing).
- Week 5: Exec-level reminder email with explicit decision deadline and consequences.

Appendix: sample metric snapshot (paste into slide)
- Month	Tokens	% change	P95 latency	Uptime
- Apr	380k	+6%	220ms	99.6%
- May	390k	+3%	200ms	99.8%
- Jun	430k	+10%	210ms	99.75%

Useful links and artifacts to attach to the email or one-pager
- Reserved capacity proposal (internal deck link)
- Production logs + SLO dashboard link
- Short case study (peer customer with similar workload)

Prep checklist for the exec sync (CSM)
- One-pager PDF exported and attached
- Top 2 technical asks cleared with Solutions Eng
- Pricing scenarios prepped and legal looped in
- Draft email ready to send after meeting

Notes to self / open questions (working items)
- Confirm whether customer procurement requires an SOW for reserved capacity (CSM to flag legal)
- Verify if on-prem networking checklist should be part of the executive packet for private deployment interest
- Ask finance for an alternative early-payment discount scenario to present as a counter-offer

—— end of doc ——
